# Story 01 — Multi-Department support (Story: STORY-017)

## Prerequisites

- None. This is the first story under the `platform` feature slug and introduces the **Department** concept. Downstream stories (Ticket Assignment, Reports, Agent scoping) will depend on this one but are out of scope here.
- Coordinate with owners of Tickets/Users/Reports before adding `DepartmentId` foreign keys on their entities — those wirings belong to their own stories, not this one.

---

## Story Goal

Introduce the **Department** aggregate as a first-class domain concept and expose a full admin CRUD REST API so that:

1. An authenticated **Administrator** can create, list, view, update and (soft) delete departments.
2. A non-Administrator receives **403 Forbidden** on any create/update/delete endpoint. Read endpoints are available to any authenticated user (needed by downstream scoping stories).
3. Other CRM entities (users, tickets, KB articles, reports) can later reference a `DepartmentId` — but wiring those references is **explicitly out of scope** for this story.

Out of scope: department-based data scoping/row-level filtering, department ↔ user membership tables, department ↔ ticket association, UI screens (frontend), Multi-Branch (FR-064).

## Product rules (from story)

Current behaviour: the system operates as a single implicit department; no `Department` entity exists.

New behaviour:
- A `Department` entity exists with a unique **Name** (case-insensitive) and an optional **Code** (short identifier, unique when supplied) and **Description**.
- Departments can be created, listed, fetched by id, updated, and soft-deleted by an Administrator.
- Non-administrators can **read** the department list (needed by dropdowns in downstream stories) but cannot mutate it.
- Deleting a department is a **soft delete** — mark inactive; downstream FKs must not cascade-fail. (No downstream FKs exist yet in this story, but design for it.)

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Domain: `Department` entity + repository interface

**Create file:** `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/Department.cs`

```csharp
namespace CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Entities;

public class Department : BaseEntity
{
    public string Name { get; set; } = default!;
    public string? Code { get; set; }
    public string? Description { get; set; }
    public bool IsActive { get; set; } = true;
}
```

- Name is required, max 100 chars.
- Code optional, max 20 chars, unique when non-null.
- `IsActive` used for soft delete; `BaseEntity` provides audit fields.

**Optional:** if the generic repository cannot express a case-insensitive uniqueness query cleanly, add `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Interfaces/IDepartmentRepository.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IDepartmentRepository : IGenericRepository<Department>
{
    Task<bool> ExistsByNameAsync(string name, Guid? excludeId, CancellationToken ct);
    Task<bool> ExistsByCodeAsync(string code, Guid? excludeId, CancellationToken ct);
}
```

Otherwise implement the uniqueness check inline in the handler using `IGenericRepository<Department>` predicates.

### 2 — Application: DTOs, commands/queries, validators, mapping

Add under `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Features/Departments/`:

- `DTOs/DepartmentDto.cs` — `Id`, `Name`, `Code`, `Description`, `IsActive`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`.
- `DTOs/CreateDepartmentRequest.cs` — `Name`, `Code?`, `Description?`.
- `DTOs/UpdateDepartmentRequest.cs` — `Name`, `Code?`, `Description?`, `IsActive`.
- `Commands/CreateDepartmentCommand.cs`, `Commands/UpdateDepartmentCommand.cs`, `Commands/DeleteDepartmentCommand.cs`.
- `Queries/GetDepartmentByIdQuery.cs`, `Queries/GetDepartmentsQuery.cs` (supports optional `includeInactive` flag; default `false`).
- Corresponding handlers per command/query.
- `Validators/CreateDepartmentRequestValidator.cs`, `Validators/UpdateDepartmentRequestValidator.cs` — FluentValidation rules: `Name` required, max 100; `Code` optional, max 20, alphanumeric; `Description` optional, max 500.

**Handler behaviour:**
- **Create:** trim `Name`; verify no active department has the same `Name` (case-insensitive) → throw `ConflictException`. Same for `Code` when supplied. Persist via `IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync`.
- **Update:** load by id → throw `NotFoundException` if missing. Re-check uniqueness excluding the current id. Save.
- **Delete:** load by id → throw `NotFoundException` if missing. Set `IsActive = false`. Do **not** hard-delete.
- **GetById:** throw `NotFoundException` if not found or soft-deleted (unless `includeInactive=true`).
- **GetList:** return `List<DepartmentDto>` ordered by `Name`.

**Create file:** `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Mappings/DepartmentProfile.cs` — AutoMapper profile: `Department` ↔ `DepartmentDto`, request DTOs → entity.

### 4 — API: `DepartmentsController`

**Create file:** `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Controllers/DepartmentsController.cs`

- Inherit from `BaseApiController`.
- Route `[Route("api/departments")]`.
- Endpoints:
  - `GET api/departments?includeInactive={bool}` — `[Authorize]` (any authenticated user). Returns `List<DepartmentDto>`.
  - `GET api/departments/{id:guid}` — `[Authorize]`. Returns `DepartmentDto` or 404.
  - `POST api/departments` — `[Authorize(Roles = Roles.Admin)]`. Body `CreateDepartmentRequest`. Returns `201 Created` with `DepartmentDto` and `Location` header.
  - `PUT api/departments/{id:guid}` — `[Authorize(Roles = Roles.Admin)]`. Body `UpdateDepartmentRequest`. Returns `200 OK` with updated `DepartmentDto`.
  - `DELETE api/departments/{id:guid}` — `[Authorize(Roles = Roles.Admin)]`. Returns `204 No Content`.
- Inject the application service directly (do not use MediatR; match the pattern in other feature stories like Plan 02, 31, 34, 35, 39, 50 that use plain services).
- Reference the role name via `CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Constants.Roles.Admin`. **Do not** hard-code `"Admin"` as a string.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Duplicate name (case-insensitive):** create/update → `ConflictException` → HTTP **409**. Enforced in the command handlers and by a unique index in `DepartmentConfiguration.cs`.
- **Duplicate code when supplied:** same as above; enforced by the filtered unique index.
- **Empty / whitespace-only `Name`:** rejected by `CreateDepartmentRequestValidator` / `UpdateDepartmentRequestValidator` → HTTP **400** via `ValidationFilter.cs`.
- **`Name` or `Code` with leading/trailing spaces:** trimmed by handler before persistence and before uniqueness checks.
- **Unicode in `Name` (e.g. Arabic “الدعم الفني”):** must round-trip correctly; the EF column must use an NVARCHAR / Unicode-capable type. Verify against `ApplicationUserConfiguration.cs` conventions.
- **Non-Admin mutating:** `[Authorize(Roles = Roles.Admin)]` returns **403**. Do not throw; let ASP.NET auth pipeline handle it.
- **Unauthenticated request:** ASP.NET returns **401** before hitting the controller.
- **Update on already soft-deleted department:** allowed (Administrator can reactivate by setting `IsActive = true` in the update body); document this behaviour inline in the handler comment.
- **Delete of an already-soft-deleted department:** idempotent; return **204** without error.
- **Get by id for a soft-deleted department without `includeInactive`:** treat as not found → **404**.
- **Concurrent create with same `Name`:** the DB unique index is the ultimate guard; catch `DbUpdateException` and translate to `ConflictException`.
- **Downstream FK not yet present:** intentional. Soft-delete design ensures no data loss when tickets/users later reference departments.

## Test Plan

Add tests under a new test project if none exists (mirror the folder structure of the source projects). Otherwise co-locate with existing tests. All new tests live under `src/BackEnd/tests/` (create the folder if it does not yet exist).

1. **Unit — `CreateDepartmentCommandHandler`:**
   - Returns new `DepartmentDto` and calls `IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` exactly once.
   - Throws `ConflictException` when a department with the same name (different casing) already exists.
   - Trims `Name` and `Code`.
2. **Unit — `UpdateDepartmentCommandHandler`:**
   - Throws `NotFoundException` when id does not exist.
   - Allows updating a soft-deleted department (reactivation).
   - Uniqueness check excludes the current id.
3. **Unit — `DeleteDepartmentCommandHandler`:**
   - Sets `IsActive = false`; never removes the row.
   - Idempotent when called on an already-inactive department.
4. **Unit — `GetDepartmentsQueryHandler`:**
   - Excludes inactive departments by default.
   - Includes them when `includeInactive = true`.
   - Result is ordered by `Name`.
5. **Unit — Validators:** happy path + all failure branches (`Name` empty, `Name` > 100, `Code` > 20, `Description` > 500).
6. **Integration — `DepartmentsController` (WebApplicationFactory + in-memory or SQLite):**
   - `POST /api/departments` as Administrator → **201**, response body matches request.
   - `POST /api/departments` as a non-Administrator role → **403**.
   - `POST /api/departments` unauthenticated → **401**.
   - `POST` duplicate name → **409**.
   - `PUT /api/departments/{id}` as Administrator → **200**; as agent → **403**.
   - `DELETE /api/departments/{id}` as Administrator → **204**; row still present with `IsActive = false`.
   - `GET /api/departments` as any authenticated user → **200** with the seeded list.
   - `GET /api/departments/{id}` with unknown id → **404**.
7. **Migration smoke test:** apply the new `AddDepartments` migration to a fresh test database and assert the `Departments` table + unique indexes exist.

Reference existing test conventions before writing (search under `src/BackEnd/tests/` if present; otherwise establish the pattern using xUnit + FluentAssertions + Moq, consistent with the .csproj references already in `CustomerSupportCRM.Application.csproj` and `CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure.csproj`).

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** `dotnet ef database update --project src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure --startup-project src/CustomerSupportCRM.API` from `src/BackEnd/`.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigrationName> --project src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure --startup-project src/CustomerSupportCRM.API`. The migration only adds a new table + indexes; no data is destroyed on rollback.
- **Half-applied state:** if the migration fails mid-way (e.g. unique index creation fails on legacy data — not possible here since the table is new), the transactional migration rolls back automatically on SQL Server. Verify by re-running `dotnet ef migrations list`.
